subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` stay a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: This PR and the competing strict-validation PR encode opposite cron lifecycle contracts, and the choice affects persisted upgrade behavior, session retention, and user-facing cron creation semantics.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted-row/load or doctor coverage for existing omitted jobs while preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Reject recurring delete-after-run
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after its Gateway/UI compatibility findings are resolved.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land only the new default and explicitly document that existing omitted recurring isolated jobs require operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted-row/load or doctor coverage for existing omitted jobs while preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans cron defaulting, SQLite store load behavior, and persisted compatibility, and Vincent Koc is the strongest recent history signal for those paths in current main.
